thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: service=serving-runtime region=us-west-2 — spike of 5xx and container restarts detected. Auto-scaler activity high. Paging on-call.
alex: seeing 50% 503s on /v1/generate, errors spike at 17:24 UTC. Logs show repeated CUDA OOM in gc-phase. Rolling restarts on worker pools.
mari: confirmed. Metrics: p95 latency up from 120ms to 2.1s, error rate 48% over last 3m. Customers reporting brownouts. @oncall-sre can you take?
oncall-sre: taking. I’m on my laptop, joining zoom. Can someone paste failing pod logs and recent scale events?
alex: pasting snippets below — noisy but shows pattern:
```
E cuda: out of memory while allocating 3.8 GiB
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/serve/runtime.py", line 412, in step
    outputs = model.generate(inputs)
  File "/lib/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1190, in __call__
    return forward_call(*args, **kwargs)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 4039681024 bytes.
```
alex: also seeing container crashloops: `RestartCount: 6` on many pods.
suresh: autoscaler events show very rapid scale-up then immediate scale-down, causing many pods to be preempted. HPA target CPU triggered by a short CPU spike from batching. Timeline:
- 17:20: scale from 8 -> 32
- 17:21: several nodes show `NotReady` then `Ready` (node flaps)
- 17:22: kubelet evicted pods, restart loops started
- 17:23: scale back to 6
This oscillation aligns with crashloops.
jordan: Could be continuous batching pushing big memory footprints. Maybe new batch config rolled at 17:10? Any deploys?
emily: there was a runtime config push at 17:08 that changed `max_batch_tokens` from 2048 -> 4096 (intent to increase throughput). Rolling update across serving-runtime pool at 17:09.
mari: oof. that explains memory pressure. We probably doubled typical KV cache size and some models are hitting allocation. Suggest two-pronged mitigation: 1) freeze autoscaler, 2) revert batch config or pin to previous model config, 3) cordon problematic nodes.
oncall-sre: executing mitigation now.
- command: `kubectl rollout pause deployment/serving-runtime -n prod` (pause rollout to stop further rolling config changes)
- command: `kubectl patch hpa serving-runtime -p '{"spec": {"minReplicas": 6, "maxReplicas": 12}}'` to limit burst scaling
suresh: I'm increasing HPA stabilization window: `kubectl patch hpa serving-runtime -p '{"spec": {"behavior": {"scaleUp": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds": 300}, "scaleDown": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds": 300}}}}'`
alex: cordoning the noisy nodes now: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-4-12` and draining low-priority pods.
jordan: rolling back batch config is safest. emily — can you push rollback to previous config (current revision r2024 -> r2023)?
emily: starting rollback to r2023 on config service. Will push to runtime with zero-downtime flag disabled to avoid triggering new autoscale events.
incident-bot: incident update: severity=sev2, impacted_customers=7 (partial brownout), mitigation_in_progress.
alex: after limiting HPA and cordon, new pods are starting with lower memory footprint. I'm still seeing a few CUDA OOMs but restart count decreasing.
mari: monitoring shows error rate dropped to 12% after config rollback and HPA limits. p95 latency down to 340ms but still elevated.
suresh: note: nodes with kernel `nvidia-ml` driver 530.41 show slightly higher OOMs vs 535.x — flagging for later infra follow-up.
oncall-sre: taking ownership for the next 30m. Handoff: I will keep HPA pinned, paused rollout, and supervisor the rollback. @alex @emily keep me posted if error rate goes below 2% for 15m, then we can re-enable autoscaler with tuned params.
jordan: quick patch proposal for permanent fix: reduce `max_batch_tokens` to 3072, enable KV prefix caching for short prompts, and add autoscaler damping factor to avoid >2x scale changes within 5m.
emily: ack. I'll open a PR for config and schedule a canary for low-traffic region first.
alex: customer comms: CS notified top 7 affected customers, standard post-incident update queued.
incident-bot: update logged. Pager duty: 2 pages, 3 on-call escalations.
mari: can we mark incident mitigated? error rate stable ~1.8% for last 10m, no new crashloops, node flaps subsided.
oncall-sre: marking mitigated. I'll keep watch for 30m then handback to normal ops.
emily: follow-up tasks created: BUG-1324 (batch config memory leak investigation), OPS-804 (autoscaler damping), INFRA-599 (gpu driver matrix analysis).
alex: thanks team. good run.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: severity downgraded to sev3, monitoring to continue. Incident thread will be archived in 24h.
